text:
maria-g: Quick question — noticed inconsistent behavior when we combine cookie-based anchors with trailing-slash normalization. Example: we have two routes, one anchored by cookie `user_tier=internal` and one default service. When requests hit `/account` vs `/account/` they sometimes choose different services.

maria-g: Config (simplified):
```
- matcher:
    host: "app.redwood.local"
    path: "/account*"
    anchors:
      cookie: "user_tier=internal"
    service: internal-account
- matcher:
    host: "app.redwood.local"
    path: "/account/transactions*"
    service: transactions-service
```
Observed: a request to `/account/transactions` with cookie `user_tier=internal` is hitting `transactions-service` instead of `internal-account`. Is path normalization happening before anchor evaluation or after? Should cookie anchors bind to the canonical path or the raw path?

kevin: We canonicalize paths (trailing slash normalization) in some parts of the infra but not consistently in the matcher code path. My read: current behavior is "match raw -> anchors -> normalize" which can cause these surprises.

kevin: Quick repro I ran:
```
curl -v -H "Cookie: user_tier=internal" "https://app.redwood.local/account/transactions"
# got 200 from transactions-service
curl -v -H "Cookie: user_tier=internal" "https://app.redwood.local/account"
# got 200 from internal-account
```

ashley: I'd expect canonicalization first: normalize `/account` and `/account/` to the same token, then evaluate anchors/weights. Otherwise anchor rules need to account for both forms which becomes messy for console UX.

ashley: Telemetry note: switching to canonicalize-first will change route attribution in logs — we'll need a migration or a clear changelog for customers using per-route billing or alerts. :warning:

ranjit: From routing semantics POV, anchors (cookie/header) are orthogonal to path shapes. We should apply normalization early so anchors are compared against the canonical route definitions. That also simplifies the console: in the route editor we can show the normalized path example and a single toggle `Normalize trailing slash`.

maria-g: Agreed. Two follow-ups: (1) do we want to make normalization opt-in (legacy default) or opt-out (normalize by default)? (2) what's the rollout plan so we don't surprise Dedicated/Private customers with assertion changes?

kevin: Proposal: default normalize=true for new customers and hosted, but respect `legacy_matching: true` in Dedicated/private by default. Provide a console rollout flag per-environment. Also emit a telemetry tag `path_normalization: true/false` on match events so we can backfill/segment.

ashley: That sounds reasonable. For console UX, add a per-route hint: "Matches both `/x` and `/x/` when normalization is on" and a tooltip linking to docs.

ranjit: For precedence: canonicalize -> compute specificity score -> apply anchors (headers/cookies) as tiebreaker -> apply service alias/weighting. This ordering avoids the / vs /foo/ ambiguity and keeps anchor semantics consistent.

maria-g: I'll open a design doc with the ordering and telemetry plan. Can someone volunteer to open the router PR that changes normalization order and adds the `path_normalization` tag?

kevin: I can take the PR. Will add unit tests for weird edgecases (multiple trailing slashes, `//`, `.` segments) and a migration test for existing match logs.

infra-bot: deploy:router-canary started by kevin — canary id c-2026-03-20 — routing changes behind feature flag `normalize_path_first`.

maria-g: Thanks :thumbsup: Please add a short note in the release notes and ping infra-security for the Dedicated config change checklist.

kevin: Will do. Opening PR and pinging @ranjit for a quick review on the specificity scoring change.

ranjit: I'll review. Also suggest adding an integration test that replays real traffic from our sampling pipeline to ensure no customer-visible regressions.

maria-g: Perfect. I'll add the doc and a console mock for the toggle. Closing loop once PR is merged.
